sides.name: Roman Republic and Italian allies (Varro, Paullus)
sides.note: Tech override per derived:tech-anchor (SOURCES.md anchor table, interpolated by year); air and cyber 0 = derived:absent-in-era. Ratings per derived:rating-rubric. Polybius 80,000 foot + 6,000 horse (86,400 incl. 10,000 camp garrison, excluded here) is followed by many modern historians (e.g. Goldsworthy); lower modern estimates (~50,000) set the low end. Field force: 55,000 heavy infantry, 15,000 velites, 6,400 cavalry. Republic manipular army mapped to archetype-classical-infantry. Command 0.4: divided consular command, Varro's deep frontal deployment. Training 0.45: many legions newly raised in 216 BCE.

sides.name: Carthage (Hannibal)
sides.note: Tech override per derived:tech-anchor (SOURCES.md anchor table, interpolated by year); air and cyber 0 = derived:absent-in-era. Ratings per derived:rating-rubric. Polybius 40,000 foot + 10,000 horse, accepted by most modern historians; +/-10% range. Gauls, Hispanics and Libyans as line, 6,000 skirmishers, 2,000 Balearic slingers, 6,000 Hispanic/Gallic heavy horse, 4,000 Numidian light horse. Hannibal's hammer-and-anvil double envelopment is mapped to macedonian-combined-arms (closest behavioural match). Command 1.0: Hannibal. Libyans partly in captured Roman mail.

outcome.note: Carthaginian victory, double envelopment. Roman field-army losses: Livy 48,200 killed + ~4,500 captured on the field (camp captives excluded because the camp garrison is not in forces); Polybius 70,000 killed. Infobox total incl. camps 67,500-80,000. Carthaginian killed 5,700 (Polybius) to 8,000 (Livy); high includes wounded at ~1:1 (derived). Ancient figures, grade C.
